title: Questions & privacy page
question: Three ways to lay out the page cleaners open from sign-in. Lock the one that reads best on a phone.

options.label: Staff handbook
options.lineage: the induction booklet a new cleaner is handed on day one
options.thesis: Numbered chapters with a contents list; every answer is a short numbered step list.
options.viewport: Title, a five-line contents list, then chapter 1 opening with its first question answered in steps.
options.risk: A long scroll; finding one answer relies on the contents list and tapping questions open.

options.label: If this happens, do this
options.lineage: the laminated quick-reference card on the cleaners' cupboard door
options.thesis: Problems on the left, the fix on the right, grouped by moment of the shift; privacy is its own notice.
options.viewport: Title, an outlined 'Location and privacy notice' card, then 'Signing in' with three problem → fix rows.
options.risk: Questions that are not problems ('How do I clock in?') read awkwardly as 'if this happens'.

options.label: Topic tiles
options.thesis: Six topic tiles first; each opens its own short page of questions.
options.viewport: Title, then six tiles: Signing in, Clocking in and out, Extra time, Photos and notes, Shifts and swaps, Privacy.
options.risk: One extra tap to reach any answer, and tiles look like an app menu rather than reading.
